content:
I fully admit that my DIY iPhone camera mod looks pretty ridiculous — but it really does make taking photos with my iPhone more practical and enjoyable.

The mod was originally something I came up with to solve a problem during a video shoot, but I ended up using it many more times after that…

One of the biggest divides in the compact camera world is whether or not you need a viewfinder. Back in the day, camera enthusiasts had strong opinions about electronic viewfinders (EVFs) versus optical ones, but EVFs are now so good that hardly anyone cares anymore.

But whether optical or electronic, viewfinders offer very real advantages over composing with the rear screen — especially when shooting in harsh sunlight. Even with screen brightness cranked all the way up, it's hard to see what you're shooting in bright sun, and you're also fighting screen reflections.

Although in London this hasn't historically been much of an issue, this summer brought a record-breaking heatwave, and honestly I feel like the last time I saw a cloud or rain was about thirty years ago.

But for me, it goes beyond that. I also feel there's a psychological difference between just seeing what's in the photo versus seeing the world around you when you take the shot. Sometimes it's exactly that difference that makes me reach for a dedicated camera rather than my iPhone.

When I was choosing a camcorder a few years ago, the Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 4K was the obvious runaway favourite, but the lack of a viewfinder gave me pause. In the end I decided it wasn't a big deal for me, since I mostly used it indoors, and when I needed it outside, rigging up a large monitor with a sun hood solved most of the problems.

But sometimes I want to use it more casually than the full monitor rig setup, so I found a simple accessory for outdoor use. It's a sun hood plus magnifying lens combo that magnetically attaches to the camera's rear screen, effectively giving you an optical viewfinder.

I had an upcoming shoot that required both the BMPCC 4K and my iPhone 16 Pro Max. I did a quick test shoot at the location, and the viewfinder accessory really helped. Since the BMPCC 4K and iPhone have very similar screen sizes, I wondered if the accessory would work just as well on the iPhone.

Of course the iPhone doesn't have magnets, but it's light enough that holding it up against the magnifying lens manually is no problem at all. I was pleasantly surprised by how well it worked, especially given that I use the Camera Control button as the shutter.

Since then I've used this accessory to take photos in all kinds of situations, and I love that it's easier to see the screen in harsh sunlight, and I also love the sense of immersion. My iPhone became my primary camera a long time ago, and with this DIY mod I feel even more like just the phone is enough a lot of the time.

Crazy or genius? Let me know in the comments. If you're in the latter camp, unfortunately the thing I bought seems to have been discontinued, and I haven't seen anything similar designed for screens larger than three inches. If you find one, drop a link in the comments.
